notes: Both outrunners mount on this plate (M4 on a 25 mm square; check your motor). Pivot bolt M8 through the lower hole.
Keeps hands and balls off the open side of the wheels; held by four M5 standoffs.
Motor-side (+y) cheek: holds the head's M8 pivot bolt; a printed foot bolts it to the turntable plate.

Guard-side (-y) cheek: holds the pivot bolt, and its rear tab carries the elevation actuator's anchor (M6 shoulder bolt). Same feet as the other cheek. The grommet hole under the pivot, between the feet, passes the actuator's lead.
Bolts to the end-tapped posts (M5) and to the fixed ring of the turntable bearing; the azimuth stepper hangs under it on four M3 screws; the home switch bracket sits on two M3 screws.
Bolts to the rotating ring of the bearing. Trimmed to a 108 mm radius so the azimuth pinion clears it at every angle; the printed gear sector bolts under its +y edge (3 x M4).
Sits on the rails (M5 and T-nuts); holds the battery and electronics.
Gearmotor (37 mm class, M3 on a 31 mm circle) bolts to the inside face. M5 into the side rail's T-slot.
608 bearing in the bore, 8 mm axle bolt. M5 into the side rail's T-slot.

Tub shelf, falls 12 deg toward the net so balls roll to the outlet. Posts bolt up through it (M5, end-tapped), the sleeve socket under the outlet hole, the agitator's motor mount under the small hole beside it.
On the two mast rails at the lift (M5 and T-nuts at the ends). The boot hangs under it on the four inner M5s; the spine passes through and is squared to it with two 2040 corner brackets.

Slip hub's pressure plates: the D bore keys them to the gearmotor's shaft; deburr both faces flat (they are the friction faces against the facings). Set the hub to 0.9 N m: on the bench, the shaft in a vice, wrap a strip of the belt teeth-in round the pulley and pull it with a luggage scale; tighten collar B until it slips at 71 N, then lock its set screw. Bed the facings in: pull the strip through about 20 slips (or hold a flight and run the lift for 10 s), then set it again; fresh facings lose tens of microns as they bed in, and every micron lost after the set costs about 0.25 N of the hub's 208 N. Check it with the scale again after 300 jams or a season.
